authority: Judgements by Claude (Claude Code) on 2026-11-08 about the engine's findings. They are not output of the Riesbeck/Beane Lisp Critic and change nothing in the recorded Critiques. No code was changed on their account.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: The rule fires on EQ and EQUAL alike. Every EQUAL compares strings (site names, the reference revision) or lists, where EQL would give wrong answers; every EQ compares symbols, keywords or the same object, where EQ and EQL agree. The engine's own text allows 'something special'.
judgements.evidence: The 21 matches in the record: e.g. (EQUAL PANEL-SITE ORIGIN) in JAVA-PANEL-CONTEXT compares site-name strings; (EQ :LOCAL-OBSERVED (GETF O :OUTCOME)) compares keywords.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: OPEN is a LET* variable in PLAN-OUTCOMES (the planned !OPEN-PANEL step); CL:OPEN is never called. Renaming the variable (e.g. OPEN-STEP) would remove the ambiguity for readers and for the rule.
judgements.evidence: Match (OPEN (FIND (QUOTE !OPEN-PANEL) PLAN :KEY (FUNCTION FIRST))) is a binding in the LET* of PLAN-OUTCOMES, dreyeck/work/fedwiki-link-resolution.lisp.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: DOMAIN-ITEMS reads the domain file with :EOF as end marker; a top-level :EOF in that file would stop the read early. The file has none today, but a fresh marker (a list made at run time) is the correct idiom. Small fix recommended.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: Fair for PLAN-OUTCOMES, CHECK-JAVA-AGREEMENT and CHECK-DISTINCTIONS: each does several separable things (outcome classification; request comparison and outcome comparison; five distinctions in one check). The other matches are single counter-probes whose length is mostly their assertions.
judgements.evidence: 14 matches; the three named functions are the longest and the most mixed.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: LINK-RESOLUTION-EXPERIMENT takes three optional arguments; &KEY would make the Inspector handoff calls readable. UNAVAILABLE is a test helper with two optionals; minor.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: Both compare the length of a list with a small constant in test code; (null (rest x)) or a length check against a bound would avoid traversing, at no gain in clarity here.
judgements.evidence: (= 1 (LENGTH OUTCOMES)) in ONLY, (= 2 (LENGTH TWO)) in CHECK-DISTINCTIONS.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: CHECK-JAVA-AGREEMENT accumulates PLANNED with SETF/APPEND inside the loop; a LOOP ... APPEND would say the same directly.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: All three are '() list initialisations, which the engine's own recommendation text calls OK.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: DOMAIN-MUTANT evaluates a SHOP3:DEFDOMAIN form built from a copy of the production domain's own source, to define a disposable mutant domain under a fresh name. DEFDOMAIN is a macro over a literal domain; this is the mutation test's mechanism, confined to the test system.

judgements.author: Claude
judgements.statement: One APPEND of a short literal list in test data construction; LIST* would be marginally more direct, with no effect on what is tested.
